newsitem.title: FRANCE: French hold 20 in Chinese immigration ploy.
newsitem.headline: French hold 20 in Chinese immigration ploy.

text.p: French police said on Friday they had arrested 20 people in a crackdown on a ring which smuggled illegal immigrants from China and held two of them for ransom.

A police spokesman said the arrests took place earlier this week after a swoop on a house in the Paris suburbs where two Chinese men, aged 29 and 20, were being held captive at gunpoint by other Chinese nationals.
The two, who had been beaten by their captors, were being fed a bowl of rice a day and threatened with death or mutilation if relatives in Italy did not pay $15,000 ransom for each.
Police said the two men had been held for about 10 days and their captors demanded an extra $1,000 a day for each day their ransom was not paid.
They had already paid the equivalent of $15,000 each before leaving China in November in order to be smuggled into France through Hong Kong, Bangkok, Vienna and Berlin, police said.
The basement of the villa in which they were held contained a clandestine workshop equipped with 21 sewing machines and facilities to summarily house workers, they said.
French authorities say they are particularly worried by Chinese gangs which smuggle in illegal immigrants and appear to be tempted to branch out into other criminal activities.
